Successful completion of the Professional Writing minor also requires the submission of a writing portfolio during a student's final semester. This portfolio must be submitted electronically to the minor advisor at pwminor@umd.edu by November 1 for fall semester graduation, April 1 for spring semester graduation, or August 1 for summer graduation. The electronic portfolio must contain, at a minimum, the following material:
A welcome page
Six finished, polished texts written by the student in Professional Writing minor courses; and
A reflective essay that analyzes how these documents demonstrate the student's achievement of the minor's learning outcomes.
The minor advisor will confirm that each portfolio meets these minimum requirements.
Notes:
Credit toward the minor will be granted for only one of these two courses: ENGL281 or ENGL384.
Credit toward the minor will be granted for only one of these two courses: ENGL281 or ENGL384.
Students cannot count toward the Professional Writing minor the PWP course that they take to fulfill the Fundamental Studies Professional Writing requirement for the University of Maryland General Education Program. Only a second PWP course can be used to fulfill the Professional Writing minor requirement. Advisors will encourage students to select a second PWP course only if it complements the students' academic or professional goals.

Students may satisfy up to three credits of the nine-credit 3xx- or 4xx-level coursework requirement through documented writing-intensive internship experience. The internship must be approved by the Professional Writing minor advisor in order to have these three credits count toward their minor.

Following university policy, English majors may count two Professional Writing minor courses toward both the requirements for the English major and the Professional Writing minor.

Undergraduate
Undergraduate Programs
Our undergraduate programs train students in key approaches to analyzing literature and media, the structures and effects of the English language, and theories and practices of writing from the creative to the professional. Find details about our B.A. program, honors program and minors.
Graduate
Graduate Programs
Our graduate programs offer an extraordinary depth and range of expertise with highly individualized professional and pedagogical mentorship. Find details about our M.F.A., M.A. and P.h.D. programs.
People
People
Meet our faculty, staff and graduate students. Our tenure-track faculty are first in their fields, with a wide-ranging and award-winning body of work in digital media, scholarly essays, and books, novels, short stories and poetry. Our professional-track faculty teach a diverse range of courses and make significant contributions to our education goals and research expertise.
Apply
Why UMD English?
Located just 10 miles from the nation's capital, we have easy access to the city’s rich cultural and scholarly resources, including the Library of Congress, the Smithsonian, the Folger Shakespeare Library and the National Archives. By enrolling in our programs, students join an exciting, diverse, engaged and thriving intellectual community.
Give
Give
The UMD Department of English takes heart in our common pursuit of literature and language as vital to crossing the boundaries of difference. It makes us discerning about language and its effects, it drives us to question ourselves and to empathize with diverse identities, and it helps us compose a better world. Your gift will make a difference in the educational experience of our students. Thank you for your generosity.

Academics
Undergraduate Studies
Minors are an excellent way for students to gain expertise in an area beyond the major. We encourage students to work with their advisors early to incorporate the minor into their Academic Plans.
Applications for all minors remain open until the minor is filled. Students will be taken on a first-come, first-served basis. When you click on the “contact form” below and select the appropriate option on the form, your request will be marked with the date and time. Please keep in mind that any pre-requisites must be completed by the time of application. (Students applying to the Music Performance minor must successfully pass an audition and should contact the advisor through the form below as soon as possible.)
When a minor is listed as CLOSED, it is closed until October 1 in the fall semester or March 1 in the spring semester. You may check this site again at these times. When a minor is listed as WAITLIST, it is closed, but you may put yourself on a waitlist by clicking on "contact form" below and selecting the appropriate option.
